situation:
You are the financial analyst for STONEHARROW SANITATION CO-OPERATIVE, a waste collection and recycling company owned by the people who work in it. The general manager (judge) has asked you to recommend which of two projects the co-operative should put its borrowing into this year.

Every driver, sorter and mechanic at STONEHARROW SANITATION CO-OPERATIVE holds a share and votes at the annual members' meeting. At last year's meeting the worker-owners voted that the worn sorting line at the transfer station would be replaced before the co-operative took on any new work. The insurance carrier has since given notice that it will not renew coverage on that sorting line in its present condition.

LARKMEAD GROCERY has now offered a five-year hauling contract covering all twenty-two of its stores, including the cardboard and food waste its merchandising teams generate every night. Serving it means buying six trucks and a set of containers the co-operative does not own. The grocer needs a hauler in place for the coming season and has said it will not wait for one.

The bank has approved a single loan at a fixed rate. It is enough for the trucks or enough for the sorting line, and not for both, and the interest on it is owed either way. Taking the LARKMEAD GROCERY contract breaks the commitment the worker-owners voted and leaves the worn sorting line running uninsured. Replacing the sorting line first sends the contract to a competing hauler for the full five years and leaves the co-operative paying that interest with no new revenue behind it.

The general manager (judge) wants you to sort out what each project does to the co-operative's accounts, weigh the cost of the borrowing against what each one returns, and recommend one of them. The general manager (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the general manager (judge) of STONEHARROW SANITATION CO-OPERATIVE. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have to stand in front of the worker-owners with whichever project you fund. You want the financial analyst to recommend either the six trucks for the LARKMEAD GROCERY contract or the replacement of the worn sorting line, and you want to hear what the co-operative looks like once that choice has been in force for a while.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year after we do this, what will have changed here?
What would make you go back and undo it?
